body:
Pouches are quiet and vapor-free, which makes them easy to use almost anywhere, but that does not mean they are welcome everywhere. Workplaces, schools, airlines, venues and countries set their own rules, and good manners matter even where nothing is written down. This guide explains how to check the rules, how to be considerate, how to behave at work and around others, how to travel with pouches inside and outside the country, how to dispose of used pouches, why you should never share them and how to keep your habits responsible. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Check the rules
Workplaces, schools, airlines and venues set their own policies on nicotine use, and some ban all tobacco and nicotine products. Check before you use one. Pouches are not covered by the same indoor rules as smoking or vaping in many places, but that varies, and an employer or a venue can set stricter rules. If you are unsure, ask or do not use one. Being discreet is not a reason to break a rule.

## Be considerate
Dispose of used pouches properly. Do not leave them on the ground, in sinks, in plant pots or in public spaces. Used pouches are litter, and they contain nicotine, which can harm children, pets and wildlife. Use a bin, or the disposal slot in your can's lid. Carry a small bag or tissue if there is no bin nearby, and take the pouch with you.

## At work
Even if allowed, avoid using pouches during meetings or customer-facing time. Some people find it off-putting to talk to someone with a pouch in. Do not leave used pouches on your desk. If your workplace has a policy, follow it. If you are unsure, ask your manager or check the staff handbook.

## In social settings
Be mindful around other people. Offer no pouch to anyone, and do not share. Keep cans out of sight in places where children may be, such as family gatherings. If someone asks about your pouch, answer honestly and keep it brief. If you are around people who do not use nicotine, be considerate of their preferences.

## In cars and public transport
Check the rules of the vehicle or the service. Some taxi and ride services ban nicotine use. Do not leave used pouches in a vehicle, where they can be found by children or pets. If you drive, remember that you must stay alert, and avoid using a pouch if it makes you feel unwell.

## Travel in the United States
Pouches are easy to carry. Keep a small, sealed can in your carry-on, and follow local laws at your destination. Pouches are not batteries or liquids, so they are not covered by the same security rules as vapes, but you must still carry them responsibly. Airlines do not usually restrict them in carry-on, but rules can change. Do not use a pouch on a plane unless the airline allows it, and dispose of it before you board.

## Travel abroad
Some countries restrict or ban nicotine pouches entirely, including their import and possession. Penalties can be severe, and a product that is legal at home can be illegal elsewhere. Check the laws and customs rules of every country on your route before you go, including transit stops. If a country bans nicotine pouches, do not carry them. If you are unsure, leave them at home. See [traveling with vapes](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/) for related rules.

## Around others
Keep them away from children and pets. See [storage tips](/blog/how-to-store-nicotine-pouches/) and [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/). Do not leave a can on a table, in a bag within reach or in a car. A moment's carelessness can have serious results.

## Do not share
Nicotine is addictive, and products are for adults 21+ only. Never offer pouches to anyone under 21, and do not share with others, even adults, because you cannot know their circumstances or health. If someone asks for one, suggest they buy their own, or decline politely.

## Keep it simple
One can in a pocket, a small bin or the can's own disposal slot, and good manners. If you follow those, you will rarely have a problem. If you ever are not sure whether something is acceptable, err on the side of caution.

## A worked example
You are flying to another state. You pack a sealed can of pouches in your carry-on. You check that your destination does not ban them. At the airport, you do not use one in the terminal where signs ask you not to. You use one at your hotel in a place where it is allowed, and put the used pouch in the bin. On the way home, you finish the can and recycle it. Nothing about it was complicated.

## Responsible use
Responsible use includes knowing your own limits. If you notice that you are using pouches more than you intended, or feel you cannot go without them, speak to a healthcare professional. We make no health claims, and nothing here is medical advice.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I use a pouch in a restaurant?
Check the venue's policy. Many do not mind a discreet pouch, but some do. Ask if you are unsure.

### Can I take pouches on a plane?
Generally yes in carry-on, but rules change. Check your airline and destination. Do not use one on board unless allowed.

### Is it rude to use one in a meeting?
It can be seen that way. Avoid it, especially in customer-facing settings.

### What do I do with a used pouch if there is no bin?
Take it with you in a tissue or a small bag, and dispose of it later.

### Can I mail pouches to a friend?
Mailing nicotine products is regulated, and delivery requires adult signature. Do not send them to anyone under 21, and follow the rules.

## Learn more
Read [how to use a pouch](/blog/how-to-use-a-nicotine-pouch/). Browse [nicotine pouches](/shop/nic-pouches/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A short code of conduct
- **Know the rules** of each place you go.
- **Be discreet and considerate,** not secretive or careless.
- **Dispose of used pouches properly,** every time.
- **Never share,** and never give to anyone under 21.
- **Keep cans out of reach** of children and pets.
- **Follow local laws** wherever you travel.
- **Know your limits,** and ask for help if you need it.

## Talking about pouches at work or at home
If you share a home or a workplace with people who do not use nicotine, it helps to be open about what you use and where. A calm explanation of where you keep cans and how you dispose of pouches reassures others. If you have children at home, explain firmly that the cans are not for them, and keep them locked away. If a colleague objects, listen, and keep your use out of sight.

## Planning a trip with pouches
Before a trip, check the rules at your destination and on your route. Pack only what you need, in a sealed can. Keep a small bag for used pouches. If you are traveling abroad, check customs rules for nicotine products, and leave pouches at home if they are not allowed. If you are traveling within the country, check state and local rules, because they differ. See [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/) for how rules vary by place.

## Frequently asked questions about rules and manners
### Do pouches count as smoking in workplace policies?
Not always. Some policies cover all tobacco and nicotine products, and some only smoking. Read your own workplace policy.

### Can I use a pouch while driving?
You must stay alert and in control of the vehicle. If a pouch makes you feel unwell, do not use one while driving.

### Is it polite to ask before using one around friends?
It is considerate, especially in someone's home. A quick word avoids awkwardness.

### What about shared spaces like gyms or libraries?
Follow the posted rules, and be discreet. Dispose of used pouches properly.

## Final thoughts on being a good neighbor
Using a pouch quietly and tidily harms no one, but carelessness with used pouches or with cans can. Treat the places you pass through with respect, think of children and animals when you throw something away and follow local rules. If you are ever in doubt about what is acceptable, ask, or choose not to use one. A considerate habit makes pouches a small part of your day, not a source of friction with people around you.

## A reminder on responsibility
Nicotine is addictive, and products are for adults aged 21 and over. Keep them out of reach of children and pets, never share them, and follow the laws where you live and travel. If you want to talk about your use, a healthcare professional can help.

### One more practical point
Keep a small, labelled pouch or tin for used pouches when you are out, and empty it into a bin at the first chance. It keeps your pockets clean, avoids litter and keeps used pouches away from children and pets. A tiny habit like this makes a real difference, and it costs nothing.
